result.title: Learning When to Transfer: Reinforcement Learning for Carbon-Footprint Modeling in New Manufacturing Domains
result.summary: Manufacturers often need to characterize a new material, process, or product before enough operating data are available to train reliable predictive models for this new, target domain. Existing manufacturing operations contain potentially useful knowledge to accelerate this characterization, but indiscriminate reuse of data from existing source domains can cause negative transfer in learning of the new, target domain when the manufacturing domains differ sufficiently. This work proposes a reinforcement-learning method for selective knowledge transfer, where its reward scores each opportunity to transfer against supervised alternatives, so negative transfer is avoided and controlled during forward prediction instead of being diagnosed afterwards. Given limited data from a new target domain, the learned policy chooses among predictors based on individual source operations, subsets of the sources, or the supervised alternatives: fully pooled sources, or target data alone. A validation gate deploys the transferred prediction only when it improves upon the supervised alternatives. The method is designed for learning variables supporting carbon accounting, as well as performance and quality outcomes. We demonstrate the approach by quantifying the embodied greenhouse-gas emissions of parts produced via material-extrusion additive manufacturing, using data from 729 experiments spanning five materials: ABS, PETG, TPU, PLA, and recycled PLA. The response combines measured fabrication electricity with polymer-specific cradle-to-gate production factors, while 22 material, process, and toolpath features characterize each experiment. In leave-one-material-out evaluation, this method achieves a mean test RMSE of 5.2 g CO2e per part, 20.00% lower than target-only training (32.5% lower when only 5-10% of the target training data are available) and 10.30% lower than indiscriminate source-target pooling.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出一种强化学习的选择性知识迁移方法：由奖励将每次迁移机会与监督基线对比，在新制造域数据稀缺时选择按单一来源、来源子集、全池化或仅目标数据训练的预测器，并用验证门控决定是否采用迁移预测；在五种材料的挤出增材制造碳排放建模（729 组实验）上留一材料评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「是否迁移、何时采用外部来源预测」的学习策略与验证门控，可能为 LVR 中何时依赖外部证据或历史状态、以及 STOP 类决策提供远领域类比线索，但需核查该门控与奖励设计能否迁移到 latent 推理状态的选择与停止判断。
